questions.q: What is the PROD schema's job in this platform?
options: It's where every developer's in-progress dbt build lands while they work
It's the one schema that has already passed Chapter 4's tests and Chapter 6's CI gate — the only schema anything business-facing is allowed to read from
It's a temporary staging area for raw CSV files before they're cleaned
It only exists inside the CI runner, never in the real Snowflake account
questions.explain: PROD holds only models that have cleared tests and CI — Power BI (Lesson 22) connects only here, never to RAW or DEV.

questions.q: Why does the GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE TABLES IN SCHEMA prod TO ROLE analyst statement matter?
options: Without it, ANALYST would need a brand-new grant every time dbt build creates a new mart in prod — FUTURE TABLES makes the grant apply automatically
It only affects tables that existed before the grant was issued
It is required before CREATE SCHEMA prod can run
It gives ANALYST write access to future tables, not just read access
questions.explain: FUTURE TABLES extends the grant to objects created after the grant itself, so newly built marts are automatically readable by ANALYST without a manual re-grant.

questions.q: How does dbt's "target" concept relate to the DEV/PROD schema split this lesson builds?
options: dbt targets have nothing to do with which schema a build lands in
A target is a named connection profile; this platform defines a dev target and a prod target, each pointing dbt build at a different Snowflake schema
Targets only control which warehouse size is used, never the schema
Every dbt project can only ever have one target, named default
questions.explain: dbt doesn't know 'dev' and 'prod' as a built-in concept — targets are the real mechanism, and Lesson 6 writes the profiles.yml that defines both.

questions.q: What would go wrong if ANALYST were accidentally granted SELECT on dev instead of only prod?
options: Nothing — dev and prod always contain identical data
Business users or Power BI could end up reading a developer's half-finished, untested model instead of a trusted, CI-verified mart
The grant would simply fail with an error and have no effect
It would automatically revoke TRANSFORMER's access to dev
questions.explain: DEV is explicitly where half-finished work lives — letting ANALYST read it would break the whole point of restricting business-facing access to PROD only.

questions.q: Why might a real team give each developer a personal schema like dev_alice instead of one shared dev schema?
options: So two developers running dbt build --target dev at the same time don't overwrite or collide with each other's in-progress models
Because Snowflake requires a unique schema name per Snowflake user account
Because TRANSFORMER can only be granted access to one schema at a time
Because shared schemas are not supported by dbt at all
questions.explain: A personal dev schema per developer avoids the real collision risk of multiple people building into the exact same schema simultaneously.
